title: Dotted Line Face Emoji 🫥: Feeling Invisible, Explained
description: 🫥 is a face drawn in dashes, as if fading out. It means feeling invisible, ignored, drained or wanting to disappear. See how it is used and what it signals.
summary: 🫥 is a face outlined in dashes with a flat expression, as though it is fading away. It means feeling invisible, overlooked or left out, wanting to disappear from an embarrassing moment, or being so drained that the sender feels barely present.
meaning: Comics and cartoons draw a dashed outline around characters who are invisible or have just vanished, and 🫥 borrows that convention. Its most direct meaning is “nobody notices me.” People send it after being talked over in a meeting, left off an invitation, or having a message go unanswered in a busy group chat. It is a low-key way to say that being ignored stung.

The second sense is wanting to vanish. After an awkward moment, such as a joke that died or a typo in an important email, 🫥 means “please let me disappear.” It sits near 🫣 and 🫠 in the family of embarrassment emojis, but it is the most withdrawn of them. The melting face makes a scene of its discomfort. The dotted face just quietly stops being there.

It also describes emotional flatness: burnout, numbness, or going through the motions. “Week three of overtime 🫥” does not mean sad or angry so much as emptied out. Some people use it when talking about depression, dissociation or introversion, because it shows absence better than a frown does. In those conversations it is usually meant seriously.

There is a lighter, practical use as well. Announcing “going 🫥 for the weekend” means logging off, hiding from notifications or laying low. Approved in 2021 and on phones from the following year, the emoji is still unfamiliar to many people, so it works best with those who already use it.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It signals feeling overlooked or deflated without starting a confrontation. A friend who sends “guess I wasn't invited 🫥” is hurt and inviting you to notice. It also follows embarrassing admissions. Paired with a joke, it is self-deprecating humor; alone after a silence, it may be a quiet request for attention.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Captions about social anxiety, being the quiet one at a party, or getting ignored by a crush use 🫥. So do posts about burnout and “low social battery.” It often appears in relatable-humor formats beginning “me when,” where the punchline is blending into the wall.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Among close colleagues it jokes about being passed over or about exhaustion near a deadline. It also marks intent to go offline: “heads down and 🫥 until this ships.” With managers or clients it is too ambiguous, and anything hinting at burnout is better said plainly.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: If someone you like sends 🫥, they probably feel awkward, shy or a bit ignored, often after a message of theirs got a slow or short reply. It is not flirtatious. It is a small show of vulnerability, and a warm, attentive response is the right answer.

Turning my phone off and going 🫥 till Monday
examples.meaning: Planning to go offline and be unreachable.

Me at parties where I only know the host 🫥
examples.meaning: Self-deprecating joke about fading into the background socially.

combos.meaning: Quietly slipping away or logging off, often from an awkward situation.
Social or physical battery is empty; the sender has nothing left.
Embarrassed and overwhelmed to the point of wanting to melt and vanish at once.
Being ghosted, or ghosting someone, with a sense of fading from the conversation.

confusedWith.difference: 😶 is a solid face with no mouth and means speechless or staying silent. 🫥 has a mouth but a dashed outline, and it means unseen or fading out. 😶 has nothing to say; 🫥 feels like nobody would hear it anyway.

🫠 dissolves into a puddle while smiling, expressing embarrassment, heat or cheerful despair. 🫥 is flatter and quieter, about absence and being ignored. Melting is a visible reaction; the dotted outline is a retreat.

😐 shares the flat mouth but has a solid outline and reads as unimpressed or annoyed with someone else. 🫥 turns inward. It is about how present or noticed the sender feels, not a judgment of what was said.

avoid: Do not use it to respond to someone else's hurt, because it can look like you are checking out of the conversation.
Avoid relying on it alone if you are seriously struggling; plain words make it far easier for people to help.
Skip it with recipients on older devices or unfamiliar with newer emojis, who may see a blank box or miss the meaning.
design: A face with small eyes and a short, flat mouth whose circular outline is drawn as a broken, dashed line. On most platforms the face is paler or more washed out than a standard yellow smiley, which adds to the fading effect. The dashed outline is the constant feature across vendors.

faqs.a: It can express feeling empty, numb or invisible, which people sometimes connect with depression. It is also used lightly for embarrassment and tiredness. If a friend sends it repeatedly or in a heavy conversation, it is worth asking how they are doing.

Usually social invisibility or awkwardness: being ignored, feeling out of place, or wanting to disappear after something cringey. It is part of relatable humor about shyness and burnout and has no hidden or coded meaning.

faqs.q: What does 🫥 mean from a girl or guy?
faqs.a: They feel overlooked, awkward or worn out. If it comes after you were slow to reply or cancelled plans, it is a mild signal that they noticed. A direct, kind response usually resolves it.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🫥 and 😶?
faqs.a: 😶 is about silence: the face has no mouth. 🫥 is about presence: the face itself is disappearing. Use 😶 when you are speechless and 🫥 when you feel unseen or want to vanish.

faqs.q: When was the dotted line face added?
faqs.a: It was approved in 2021 in the same release as 🫠, 🫣, 🫢 and 🫡, and became available on major phone systems during the following year.
